behavior: A disabled field has no validity from each source: `valid` is `null`, no part has `data-invalid`, the control has no `aria-invalid`, and no `Field.Error` shows. This holds for a disabled `Field.Root`, for a field in a disabled fieldset and for a control that its own `disabled` prop disables, also with the `invalid` prop and with an error of a `Form`. A disabled control gives its form no value, and `:invalid` of CSS never matches it, so one style rule covers the two states. The browser and `validate` do not validate a read-only control, because the HTML Standard bars it from constraint validation. A read-only control shows the `invalid` prop and an error of a form, because the form submits its value. Base UI keeps `data-invalid` on a disabled field for the `invalid` prop and for an error of a form, and it shows the error of a form in a field whose control is disabled.
